newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Camet sees cenbank buying $900 mln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Camet sees cenbank buying $900 mln in 1996.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress Wednesday he estimated the Central Reserve Bank's foreign currency buying this year on the local exchange market would total $900 million.
He said this was necessary to achieve the government's goal for an average exchange rate in 1996 of 2.40 soles to the dollar.
The central bank has been intervening in the local market this year to maintain a gradual depreciation of the sol.
The sol began the year at 2.30 to the dollar and is currently trading at 2.485.
The government has predicted an average annual rate of 2.70 soles to the dollar next year in its 1997 budget proposal.
